Department Alert
Reappraisal Project
Lucas Co Assessor, Alyson Palmer, is announcing that door-to-door inspections of all residential, commercial, and industrial properties in Lucas Co will begin approximately May 26, 2026.
A reappraisal project was approved by the Conference Board in February 2023.
The purpose of the project is to equalize property assessments so that each taxpayer is responsible for paying only his/her fair share of the property tax burden. Periodic inspections and reappraisal of properties is necessary, as all types of properties do not increase or decrease in value at the same rate. Some properties physically deteriorate faster than others, and in many instances similar properties located in different areas of the county will differ greatly in value due to economic factors.
Data collectors with photo ID signed by the assessor will attempt to make interior and exterior inspections of all properties. They will be compiling information to be used to estimate the fair market value of each property. Information to be collected includes type of construction, type of interior finish, physical condition of the property, age of structures and exterior measurements. A complete sales analysis, local construction costs, and economic conditions are also considered. No estimate of value will be given at the time of inspection.
Property owners are asked to cooperate by allowing a complete inspection of their property and providing accurate information so that a fair and equitable assessment may be determined for each property.
The preliminary data collection process will begin in late May or early June, 2026. The project is scheduled for completion December 31st, 2027.
Notice of final value estimates will be mailed to each property owner after January 1, 2028. The property owners will have an opportunity to meet informally to discuss their revaluation in the spring of 2028.
The new assessed values will be effective for January 1st, 2028, for taxes payable in fiscal 2029-2030.
Representatives of Vanguard Appraisals, Inc., in conjunction with the Lucas County Assessor’s Office will be conducting this project.
All law enforcement agencies as well as the Lucas County Assessor’s Office will be apprised of the areas where data collectors are working. They will also have a listing of all names and license plate numbers of anyone involved in the project.
If any property owner has questions regarding the reappraisal project, they are urged to contact the Lucas County Assessor’s Office at 641-774-4411, extension 2, or email: palmera@lucasco.org
The Iowa Department of Revenue recommends having a complete revaluation every 10 years.
Vanguard Appraisers will knock on door.
If not home:
They will measure exterior and try to come back in the next few days to get ahold of you
If not home the second time they will leave a door hanger to set up appointment or to call to let them know about your property
If home:
Vanguard appraiser will introduce themselves and will be wearing ID
They will ask to conduct an interior/exterior review
If both are accepted they will do them
If you don’t want in home but allow exterior
Appraiser will ask you questions about interior finishes, bathrooms, bedrooms, etc
They will then complete the exterior
If you say no to both
Appraiser will leave but will take pictures from the road and information from road
They will have to estimate property information and look at other sources to come up with a value
Responsibilities of the owner
Iowa Code 428.1 & 441.19 - Property Owners have a responsibility under these codes to assist the assessor in listing their property.
Assistance can be a full inspection, conversation at the door or over the phone
Iowa Code 441.24(1) it is the property owner’s legal responsibility to report to the assessor changes or improvements to their real estate
Responsibilities of the assessor
Iowa Code 441 we must list and value all real property.
Keep Records up to date and valued at market value every 2 years
All with the assistance of the property owner.

Important Dates
January 1 - Effective date of current assessment
April 1 - Assessment Notices mailed to the property owner
April 2 - April 30 inclusive - Protest of assessment period for filing with the local Board of Review
May 1 thru adjournment - Board of Review meets each year
October 16 - October 25 inclusive - Protest period for filing with the Board of review on those properties affected by changes in value as a result of the Director of Revenue Equalization Orders (odd-numbered years)
July 1 - The filing deadline for Homestead Credit, Business Property Tax Credit, Disabled Veterans Credit, and Military Exemption. Credit and exemption will appear on the tax statement received the following year.
